rated_messages.input_message: If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, keep a pen and paper nearby to occupy your hands with doodling rather than smoking.

Recent research has found that people who use self-talk when they try not to smoke (e.g. telling yourself 'you can do it') are more successful than people who don't. It might seem a bit strange, but talking to yourself like this appears to really help.
No need to get rid of these feelings or control them with a smoke. They are not permanent.
One way to combat any urges is to keep your mouth busy - some people find that chewing sugar free gum, mints, or even a pen can be a good alternative.

If you get any urges tonight, why not confront them head on? Ask the urge - what's it going to give you? It's not going to make you richer, or better looking, and it's not going to leave you if you give in either!
Crumple a piece of paper into a ball and imagine it is your urge. Toss the "urge" into the garbage or against the wall. By doing this, you are letting go of your urges.
Notice what is triggering your urge. Have understanding and kindness for yourself for feeling this urge. It isn't easy, but can you choose to let it be there without smoking?
Think about times in the past when you have let urges pass during a stressful moment, and notice what helped make that moment easier.
Stop! Breathe. What is going on around you? Inside you? Allow everything to be just as it is. Breathe again.
Are you willing to let this urge pass for the sake of living a good long time with the people who matter most to you? When you have an urge, think about the people most important to you.
